evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry reports that Shuowen’s headform for 票 was 𤐫, glossed “fire flying,” and says the lower 火 became 示 through clerical transformation. It records later uses meaning shaking, light movement, and nimble/rapid, citing Han shu passages and Tang commentator Yan Shigu; its separate paper-money examples are from Qing and later works. Those examples do not establish a direct semantic path from fire to paper credentials or tickets.
evidence.title: [A02895] 票 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解; 《說文》; 字形資料
evidence.text: The entry says 票 was written 𤐫, with upper [𦥑囟] and lower 火, later reduced above to 覀 and with 火 miswritten as 示 in the clerical form. It gives “fire flying/rising” as the basic sense and cites the Shuowen gloss. Its cited transmitted and excavated-text examples support later senses of light movement and rapidity, including a Shuihudi Qin 日書甲種 slip 57 example 票風 (“strong/rapid wind”). It also cites Ming-era uses for documentary tickets or credentials and later banknotes. These examples do not prove a direct semantic bridge from the flame sense to credentials.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary calls 𤐫 the original form of 票 and cites Guangyun’s statement that 𤐫 means “fire flying” and is now written 票. The entry also notes distinct sound and sense connections for 𤐫 in other variant records; those do not establish a phonetic component in 票. This supports a graphic predecessor and clerical change, not the dossier’s specific two-pairs-of-hands or sparks narrative.
evidence.title: [A02895-002] 𤐫 (票) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: The exact file page describes 票-seal.svg as a drawing of 票 in Shuowen seal-script style, identifies Sinica Database and other character resources as source leads, and links its original SVG. The file page releases the modern vector representation into the public domain. It is a modern redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact.

search_audit.outcome: Located a Han shu text resource and inspected scholarly and official dictionary examples for early motion senses and later documentary or paper-money senses. The dictionary pages provide citations; a secure earliest attestation for ticket or ballot was not established.

gaps: No securely verified oracle-bone or bronze attestation for 票/𤐫 was established in this search. The dictionary sources inspected support Shuowen’s form and later Qin-slip examples, but the exact oldest artifact attestation remains unresolved.

The upper graphic element [𦥑囟] is not independently identified here as a particular object or action. The paired-hands/bag/basket and sparks explanations in the dossier are unsupported by the inspected pages.

No sound component is established by the inspected sources. The local modern and Baxter–Sagart readings are recorded separately; they do not establish a historical sound role for 覀 or another visible part.

The semantic relationship between leaping fire and the later light/rising or rapid-motion senses is plausible in the dictionaries’ accounts but is not independently demonstrated as a dated chain. The Qin-slip 票風 reading is reported by CUHK; a different Shuihudi phrase 票行 is disputed in the dossier and is not used here as secure corroboration.

No secure earliest attestation for 票 meaning a paper slip, credential, ticket, or ballot was established. The checked dictionaries provide Ming-to-later documentary examples and Qing-or-later banknote examples; dictionary order is not treated as chronology.
The Unicode Unihan character-specific page at the supplied endpoint returned an access error. No official Unicode record contents were verified during this pass.

Xiaoxuetang’s record page did not expose a specific glyph image URL through the inspected web rendering, and its official rights notice was not verified. The selected glyph candidate is therefore the Commons reconstruction only.
No repeated-source reuse assessment or extract recommendation was made; the evidence was used as character-specific paraphrase.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script form (editorial reconstruction; not a dated artifact)
items.caption: Modern vector reconstruction of the 票 form in Shuowen seal-script style. The dictionary record describes the older graph 𤐫 as “fire flying”; this drawing illustrates the seal-script tradition and is not an artifact photograph.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style outline of 票, shown as a modern vector reconstruction.
items.selection_reason: The Commons description page identifies the exact character and script style, provides the original SVG link, and states public-domain terms. It offers a usable visual for the dictionary’s reported Shuowen form without presenting the drawing as an archaeological object.
items.rights: Public domain release stated on the file page for the modern SVG representation.

limitations.text: This image is a modern vector reconstruction in Shuowen seal-script style, not a photograph or facsimile of a dated excavated artifact. No securely identified oracle-bone or bronze image was selected.
